title: Director, Early Clinical Development - CNS
description:
The Director will lead activities related to Early Clinical Development (ECD) essential to the growth of Otsuka’s discovery and early phase pipeline within OPDC’s Early Development Organization (EDO). Reporting to the ECD CNS Therapeutic Area Head, this Director is a strategic scientific and clinical leader accountable for the end-to-end early clinical development strategy and execution for Otsuka's early phase portfolio, with emphasis on CNS, particularly psychiatry, neurodegenerative disease, and neuroinflammation. The role shapes program strategy from indication selection through early clinical development (pre-IND through first-in-human and clinical proof of concept) and go/go no decisions based on clinical and/or biomarker driven endpoints ensuring seamless integration across discovery, nonclinical, clinical pharmacology, regulatory, and commercial functions. The Director, ECD - CNS, in alignment with the ECD therapeutic area head and functional head VP, collaborates with EDO senior leaders to identify, introduce, and implement translational tools or studies for early phase programs and establish strategic plans and objectives.

  
  

This position can be based remotely or as a hybrid role in Princeton, NJ, Rockville, MD or Waltham, MA. Travel is expected 20% of the time based on business needs.

  

**Key Responsibilities:**

* Serve as scientific and clinical expert in CNS translational medicine and early clinical development, contributing to strategic program decisions; serve as ECD lead on development teams for multiple assets.
* Drive Research-to-Development (R2D) strategies and stage-gate decision-making, including indication prioritization and go/no-go based on mechanistic rationale, benefit-risk, and clinical unmet need as well as on clinical and/or biomarker driven endpoints. Prepare and present decision-quality data packages for internal governance reviews to support stage-gate decisions.
* Interact with internal and external groups to evaluate new compounds, molecular and biological targets as well as new formulation technologies.
* Partner with internal and external research organizations to expand and facilitate development of early phase and discovery phase compounds. Engage with external experts and key opinion leaders to inform translational and Proof of Concept (PoC) strategy and maintain scientific leadership.
* Represent ECD in cross functional as well as internal/external collaborations (BD, etc.) on activities related to early phase target and asset identification. Support regulatory interactions (e.g., pre-IND, IND submissions) and ensure translational strategies align with regulatory requirements.
* Lead scientific and clinical development efforts for assigned programs from target identification through IND and proof-of-concept. Provide medical leadership for early-phase clinical protocols, informed consent forms, and investigator brochures; monitor safety and contribute to DSMB or safety review activities as needed.
* Support or lead or public-private partnerships operating in pre-competitive settings to advance internal clinical development capabilities.
* Interact with other disciplines within the EDO to promote, initiate and elevate cross-functional early development activities. Collaborate with biomarker and digital innovation teams to develop and implement biomarker-driven approaches for CNS programs.
* Support the development of team members to build translational and early clinical development expertise.
  

  

**Qualifications:**

**Required**

* MD, MD/PhD, or PhD with subspecialty training in Clinical psychology/neuropsychology
* 5+ years of translational medicine and/or early clinical development experience with a track record of advancing biologics and/or small molecules through IND and FIH/PoC.
* Expert understanding of industry best practices and adjacent functional areas.
* Demonstrated ability to coordinate and guide cross-functional teams in matrixed, global setting, with solid strategic thinking and the ability to make informed decisions amid uncertainty.
* Outstanding communication skills with the ability to synthesize complex data and influence executive stakeholders.

**Preferred**

* MD with specialty training in psychiatry and/or neurology.

* Deep expertise in CNS, particularly psychiatry, neurodegenerative disease, and/or neuroinflammation.
* Experience implementing clinical study plans to drive decision-making.
* Experience with external collaborations.
  

  

**Competencies**  
**Accountability for Results -** Stay focused on key strategic objectives, be accountable for high standards of performance, and take an active role in leading change.
  
**Strategic Thinking & Problem Solving -** Make decisions considering the long-term impact to customers, patients, employees, and the business.
  
**Patient & Customer Centricity -** Maintain an ongoing focus on the needs of our customers and/or key stakeholders.
  
**Impactful Communication -** Communicate with logic, clarity, and respect. Influence at all levels to achieve the best results for Otsuka.
  
**Respectful Collaboration -** Seek and value others’ perspectives and strive for diverse partnerships to enhance work toward common goals.
  
**Empowered Development -** Play an active role in professional development as a business imperative.

**Job Summary:**

The Lina lab investigates innovative therapeutics, biomaterials, and diagnostic tools to further our understanding of laryngotracheal stenosis, a group of disorders that result in airway obstruction. We use patient-derived clinical samples and in vivo surgical models to further our understanding of the pathophysiology of airway stenosis and laryngeal scar and develop treatment models with real-world clinical applications.

**General Description**
=======================

Will be part of a clinically driven translational research laboratory studying injury and wound healing in the larynx and trachea and developing tissue engineering strategies to treat the disease. Under the general supervision of a faculty investigator, this position is responsible for independently performing routine experiments in the research laboratory and contributing to general maintenance of the laboratory, equipment, supplies, and animal colonies. Work requires an advanced understanding of immunological methods, immunohistochemistry, experimental design, basic understanding of statistical methods, and techniques gained through previous training and experience.

**Examples of Duties Performed**

* Utilize *in vivo* animalmodels in experiments. Follows experimental protocols, monitors animal safety and maintains health in accordance with USDA and AALAC guidelines. Administrating anesthesia, sacrificing and dissecting animals as required. Prepares tissue for study utilizing biochemical and histochemical techniques.

* Operates basic laboratory equipment such as centrifuge, analytical balance, incubator, spectrophotometer, flow cytometer, microscopy, and/or utilizes laminar flow hood.

* Will keep accurate and up-to-date records of experiments performed. Expected to become familiar with computer ordering system.

* Operates lab computers for data entry. Maintains accurate data records.

* Prepare lab for daily operations, including stocking materials, equipment, safety, cleanliness, and related areas

* Dispose of laboratory materials and samples using well-established guidelines and instructions

* Review and implement lab support policies, practices, and programs to meet organizational, operations, and management needs

* Assist Team Leads, Supervisors and/or management with creation and implementation of processes and procedures and quality improvement initiatives

* Independently review, develop, and implement new or modified laboratory techniques required for research projects

* Experiments will involve propagation of tissue culture, PCR, immunohistochemical staining of cells and tissue, and small animal husbandry. Expected to manage mouse census and care for animals according to protocols.

**Professional Development Opportunities**  
Training in the Lina Lab supports postdocs and PhD scientists in pursuing academic or non-academic careers. Scholars will have access to tailored professional development, including:

* Funding for annual attendance and presentation at a national conference.

* Opportunities to engage with clinicians

**Description**
---------------

**University of Colorado Anschutz**

**Department: School of Medicine – Department of Orthopedics**

**Job Title: Assistant Professor**

**Position #: 00854152 – Requisition #: 41491**

**Job Summary:**

The position involves the development and sustained growth of an independent, externally funded research program focused on osteoarthritis, fracture healing, and the musculoskeletal implications of the gut microbiome. The successful candidate will establish and lead an innovative research laboratory within the Research Section of the Department of Orthopedics at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus. The candidate is expected to develop a nationally recognized research portfolio, secure extramural funding with an emphasis on NIH and other federal funding mechanisms, and foster multidisciplinary collaborations across basic, translational, and clinical science domains.

Research activities should advance the understanding of musculoskeletal disease mechanisms and therapeutic strategies, with opportunities to leverage the extensive research infrastructure and collaborative environment of the Anschutz Medical Campus. The successful candidate will mentor graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, research staff, and trainees; contribute to the academic mission of the department; and participate in institutional initiatives that promote scientific innovation, team science, and translational impact. The candidate will be expected to disseminate research findings through high-impact peer reviewed publications and national and international scientific presentations, while building a sustainable program that enhances the department's reputation as a leader in musculoskeletal research.

**Key Responsibilities:**

* **Develop, conduct, lead, and disseminate innovative research aligned with the Department of Orthopedics' research mission.**This includes designing and executing independent research studies; establishing and leading a productive research program; presenting findings at local, national, and international scientific meetings; and publishing results in high-impact, peer-reviewed journals. Responsibilities also include developing competitive grant proposals and securing extramural funding from the NIH, other federal agencies, foundations, and industry partners to support a sustainable and growing research enterprise.

* **Provide education, mentorship, and training across the academic spectrum.**This includes teaching and mentoring undergraduate students, medical students, graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, orthopedic residents, clinical fellows, and other trainees. The successful candidate will provide scientific expertise, supervision, constructive feedback, career development guidance, and leadership, while actively participating in and leading educational seminars, journal clubs, workshops, and community outreach activities.

* **Foster a culture of collaboration, teamwork, professionalism, and accountability within the Department of Orthopedics and the Research Section.**This includes promoting interdisciplinary research initiatives, nurturing productive scientific relationships among faculty, trainees, and staff across all divisions of the department, and contributing to an inclusive and supportive research environment. The successful candidate will be expected to actively engage in collaborative team science efforts and help advance the department's strategic research goals.

* **Contribute to the growth and visibility of the Department's research enterprise.**This includes participating in institutional and departmental committees, supporting strategic research initiatives, developing new collaborative opportunities across the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, and enhancing the national and international reputation of the Department of Orthopedics through scholarly achievement, leadership, and service.

* **Lead and manage an independent research laboratory.**Responsibilities include recruiting, supervising, and mentoring research personnel; managing laboratory operations and budgets; ensuring compliance with institutional, regulatory, and funding agency requirements; and maintaining the highest standards of scientific rigor, reproducibility, and research integrity.

**Work Location:**

Onsite – this role is expected to work onsite and is located in Aurora, CO.

**Why Join Us:**

The University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus is one of the nation's leading academic health centers, bringing together nationally recognized programs in medicine, nursing, pharmacy, public health, dental medicine, and graduate biomedical sciences. The campus supports a robust community of researchers, clinicians, educators, and trainees engaged in collaborative discovery and translational science. The CU Anschutz School of Medicine recently ranked **No. 8 among public medical schools and No. 21 overall nationally in NIH funding**, its highest ranking in two decades, demonstrating the institution's strong commitment to research excellence and scientific innovation. The Department of Orthopedics is consistently ranked among the nation's leading orthopedic research programs, providing an exceptional environment for investigators pursuing impactful musculoskeletal research.

The Anschutz Medical Campus is also recognized nationally for the strength of its educational and research programs. The School of Medicine is designated a **Tier 1 Research Medical School** by U.S. News & World Report and is part of a campus that includes numerous nationally ranked graduate and professional programs. The campus is home to extensive core facilities, research centers, clinical research infrastructure, and multidisciplinary collaborations that support investigators from basic discovery through clinical translation and implementation.
